opportunities.title: APEX Awards

amount.raw: Applicants can apply for up to £200,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must be an exceptional independent researcher with strong track record and proven ability to lead collaborative work, hold a permanent or fixed-term position covering the award duration, have teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved, and be based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Up to two Co-applicants from different Academy remits.
opportunities.summary: APEX Awards (Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research) offer established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary and blue-skies, curiosity-driven research to benefit wider society, in partnership with the Royal Society and the Royal Academy of Engineering and supported by the Leverhulme Trust. Awards up to 24 months, commencing between 1 October and 31 December 2027, with up to £10,000 for public engagement costs.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; no prior British Academy funding required. Successful recipients expected to have some prior public engagement experience. Previous successful recipients are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a GLAM organisation (gallery, archive, library, museum) or performing arts organisation. Awards up to £8,000 to deliver innovative public engagement projects between 1 April 2027 and 31 December 2028.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Eligible applicants must be early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany, in the humanities and social sciences. Evaluated on research interest in the theme, commitment to interdisciplinary engagement, and career development potential.
opportunities.summary: Research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', bringing together around fifteen early career researchers from the UK and fifteen from Germany across the humanities and social sciences, taking place 21-23 April 2027. Symposium covers travel, accommodation and visa costs, with seed funding available for international collaborations.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of doctorate origin; anyone with a UK doctorate eligible. Early career stage, viva completed between 1 Apr 2024 and 1 Apr 2027. No permanent academic post held. Funded by DSIT.
opportunities.summary: Three-year award to an annual cohort of outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards completion of a significant piece of publishable research. Funded at 80% of FEC salary, directly allocated and indirect costs. Tenable for three years from Autumn 2027.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead Applicant must be ordinarily resident in the UK, hold a current long-term appointment at a UK-based HEI or IRO continuing for the full duration of the award, and intend to pursue original independent research within the Humanities or Social Sciences. Co-applicants may be based in the UK or overseas.
opportunities.summary: Scheme promoting acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas (quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages) by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination. Awards up to £10,000, held for 6-12 months, commencing between 1 March and 31 March 2027.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: Up to £300,000 over 2 years at 80% FEC

opportunities.eligibility_summary: PI must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute holding an established role lasting at least the award duration, of postdoctoral or above status, spending at least 20% of time on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants required. Interdisciplinary collaboration across SHAPE and STEM disciplines required.
opportunities.summary: Supports projects led by UK-based researchers in the humanities and social sciences working with international partners on genuinely interdisciplinary projects across SHAPE and STEM disciplines on the theme of Mobilities. Funding up to £300,000 over 2 years at 80% FEC, projects beginning March/April 2027.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: Awards for up to £150,000 for 12 months (with FEC at 80%)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences. Applicants must demonstrate solid understanding of relevant issues and policy landscape; language skills desirable but not essential.
opportunities.summary: Provides opportunities for UK-based early and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to develop skills, networks and careers in the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors. Up to two one-year fellowships hosted in DGAP's offices in Berlin, addressing challenges requiring innovative approaches. Areas include security/defence, Indo-European relations, technology and AI, and strategy-making in Europe. Commencing by September 2027.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs

amount.raw: Funding of up to £4,000 to support additional needs

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available for current British Academy award-holders or applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months. If not a current award-holder, must identify the scheme they intend to apply for and meet its eligibility requirements.
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require, in addition to the amount already requested for research expenses. Covers specific equipment to overcome barriers for disabled researchers, assistance for those with sensory impairments, caring costs for research trips, and support making applications. Reviewed on a rolling, case-by-case basis.
